title: Trustworthy Text-to-Image Diffusion Models: A Timely and Focused Survey

bias_targets.methodology: The paper reviews methods that analyze the co-occurrence of gender with specific attributes (e.g., occupations like firefighters), measure the likelihood of gender-marked words in generated captions, and calculate diversity scores across gender groups in benchmarks.

The paper discusses metrics such as Stereotype-Distribution-Total-Variation (SDTV) to quantify racial stereotypes (e.g., associating specific racial groups with poorer housing) and reviews benchmarks like DALL-EVAL that assess social bias in terms of race.
The paper evaluates methods that measure cultural shifts in generated images induced by non-Latin homoglyphs in text prompts using VQA Scores and Relative Bias metrics.
The paper surveys benchmarks like ENTIGEN that evaluate image generation changes and diversity scores when using prompts with ethical interventions related to skin color.
The paper reviews methodologies for detecting association-engendered stereotypes, such as measuring the total variation distance between stereotype probability distributions for sensitive attributes.
